text:
marta: FYI LATAM-GPU pool degraded ~40% due to node reboot storms in gce-ll01, traffic shifting started but we hit DNS propagation lag. Lowering TTL now?

samir: saw increased 5xxs from region, autoscaler couldn't spin up because quota. switching traffic to us-west via steer is in progress.

marta: Current authoritative TTL is 1800s... sigh. Can't wait that long.

nora: We can push TTL to 30s but majority of public resolvers clamp to 300s (corporate proxies sometimes clamp higher). Expect partial propagation variance.

james: Also remember negative effect: query spike and potential DNS egress cost. Estimate ~2-3x QPS for 5-10 minutes if we ramp TTL down.

eng-infra-bot: healthcheck LATAM-GPU: failing (5m avg CPU 90%)

marta: plan: 1) lower TTL to 60s 2) create a new delegated subdomain to prime around new targets 3) initiate steer to us-west 4) monitor resolver clamp rate + error budget

samir: why a new delegated subdomain? won't priming existing records suffice?

marta: priming helps but when resolvers clamp or have sticky NS caches, existing A records can remain. Creating traffic-ttl.redwood-internal with new NS lets us bypass cached delegations; we'll CNAME app.redwood.ai -> traffic-ttl.redwood-internal and switch delegation. It's a small window but more reliable than relying on TTL alone.

nora: Alternative: point a short-lived ALIAS/ANAME at our anycast traffic manager (if provider supports instant changes). Not all registrars/hosts support that, so we need fallback. Also check EDNS0 behavior for large ISP resolvers.

james: If we create a new delegation, make sure wildcard certs cover it and that our synthetic monitoring probes use the new name. Any cert gaps would make this worse.

ops-bot: reminder: update monitoring checklist for delegated names / cert verification

samir: concerned about quota and scaling on the traffic manager when we prime with lots of queries. Could create backpressure on control plane.

nora: For priming, use distributed clients from our vantage network to warm caches, not external mass queries. Also throttle priming to avoid hitting provider limits.

marta: short-term actions: lowering TTL to 60s now, create delegation and CNAME in 5m, start progressive steer to us-west (40% -> 80% -> 100%). Watch resolver-clamp metric and dns-qps.

james: set alert: dns-ttl-clamp-rate > 10% for any major resolver class -> rollback TTL change and escalate.

samir: opening a cloud quota ticket to allow faster scale-up, linking to the incident.

nora: after service stable, revert TTL to 1800 and write postmortem including resolver-clamp matrix per vendor and the "delegate-and-prime" playbook. I'll own the write-up.

marta: ACK. rolling TTL now: api.* = 60s, edge.* = 60s. Recording change in incident log.

eng-incident-bot: change recorded by marta at 1991203480

marta: any blockers from cert/monitoring?

james: certs/wildcard OK, monitors will follow new name after probe config push.

samir: starting steer now: routing weight -> us-west 40% (1991203520), then 80% (1991203550)

nora: seeing expected DNS QPS spike from priming: +3x for the 60s windows. No provider rate limits triggered.

marta: 5xxs trending down in latam. continuing to monitor latency and error rates. :thumbsup:

samir: FYI one corporate resolver returning old IPs (observed TTL clamp=900s). Added to follow-up list for postmortem.

marta: noted. postmortem action item: include vendor resolver clamp matrix + recommended mitigation (delegate-and-prime, anycast fallback, monitoring).

nora: I'll own postmortem and follow-ups. tagging @marta @samir @james for action items.

marta: thanks team. will close thread when services stable and follow-ups filed.
